newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNPAP ACTIVITIES WOUND UP AT YEAR-END.
newsitem.headline: FINNPAP ACTIVITIES WOUND UP AT YEAR-END.

text.p: The activities of Finnpap, a marketing association run by Finnish paper producers, are being wound up at the end of 1996 in line with an earlier decision, forestry group UPM-Kymmene said on Tuesday.

"(Finnpap's) corporate format will change in January to that of a joint stock company, after which UPM-Kymmene will buy Metsa-Serla's and Myllykoski's stakes in the company to be formed," UPM said in a statement.
The sale of Finnpap's marketing network to UPM-Kymmene and the plan to end joint marketing operations by the end of 1996 was announced in January 1996.
The continued operations of the new company, Finnpap Oy, as a subsidiary of UPM-Kymmene would be mainly technical, UPM said.
Finnpap, founded in 1918 and with assets worth 200 million markka, would handle the collection of certain receivables and would retain stakes in UPM-Kymmene sales and transport units, UPM said.

The European Commission stipulated that joint marketing activities had to be dismantled as a condition for approval of the 1996 merger between Kymmene Oy and Repola Oy, which created UPM-Kymmene, the company said.
The dismantling of the joint marketing association had been carried out in understanding with the other member organisations, UPM said.
